title: Afterglow deploy slate and shift protocols (draft)
content:
Context:
This is a compact, practice-first deploy slate for the ‘afterglow’ deployment lane — small feature slices rolled out during the late-evening quiet window after heavy traffic days. The goal: low-risk activation of model-routing tweaks, batching/kv-cache config changes, and minor runtime patches that benefit tail-latency and cost without broad user-facing changes.

How this doc is used:
- Primary: ops shift lead (night) runs preflight and coordinates the roll.
- Secondary: SRE and Serving Runtime engineers consult the rollback matrix and telemetry thresholds.
- Use this as the single source during the 4h window; post-flight notes should be pasted to CONFLUENCE-REL-5678.

Owners and roles:
- Shift lead: Maya Patel (owner)
- Runtime on-call: Owen Zhang
- Model routing/QA: Priya Kumar
- Observability/SLOs: Leo Martínez
- Communications: Release comms (team alias: #releases)

Preflight checklist (run 90–60 min before window):
- [ ] Confirm quiet window reserved, no mock traffic jobs scheduled (calendar check).
- [ ] Verify Dedicated pool headroom >= 30% for canary (console -> Dedicated -> pool-23).
- [ ] Snapshot current model routing map (api: GET /v1/routing/map -> save JSON).
- [ ] Snapshot batching and cache profiles (console -> Optimize -> active profiles).
- [ ] Export latest traffic heatmap for preceding 6h (observability -> heatmaps -> export).
- [ ] Validate rollback playbook available on primary pager.
- [ ] Confirm Slack channel #release-afterglow and on-call attendees.
- [ ] Ensure runbook runner has creds to trigger canary and model-fallback (keys scoped: deploy:canary).

Canary plan (15–30 min canary; expand if stable):
- Phase A (canary, 15m): 0.5% traffic -> routing rule: add new batching hint profile (batch-window=8ms, prefetched-kv=true) to a single canary hostgroup.
  - Command: deploy-tool canary --group canary-AG-03 --config batching_hint=afterglow-8ms --traffic 0.5
  - Observability check: latency p50/p95 change < +5ms, error-rate delta < 0.1%
- Phase B (cardinality test, 15m): increase to 5% if Phase A stable. Warm KV caches using synthetic prefix requests (script: tools/warm_kv_afterglow.sh).
- Phase C (gradual ramp, 20–40m): if Phase B stable, ramp to 25% then 50% over 20m, monitoring for model-quality regressions.

Rollout calendar (UTC):
- T-90m: preflight starts (see checklist)
- T-60m: final readiness sync, annotate any outstanding issues
- T-30m: lock release branch and tag (runtime PR merged: #2183)
- T-15m: start Phase A canary (0.5%)
- T+15m: if green -> Phase B (5%) and run synthetic KV warmers
- T+35m: if green -> Phase C (25% -> 50%)
- T+75m: full evaluation window; team decides to continue or abort
- T+120m: postflight notes and retrospective draft posted

Telemetry and guardrails (signals to watch):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 across endpoints; alert if p95 increases > 10% absolute or > 20ms
- Errors: API error rate and model-inference errors (tokenization/model-serve failures) -> alert if increase > 0.2%
- Cost: per-token cost estimate (Dedicated pool metering) -> flag if projected cost increases > 8% over baseline (run cost-estimator script)
- Quality: automatic eval on sample prompt set (eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/afterglow-set) -> flag if rouge/emd deviate beyond configured thresholds
- Cache hit-rate: prefix/KV hit-rate should trend up after warmers; if it drops, pause rollout

Quick rollback matrix (decision ladder):
- Soft pause: if any signal crosses warning threshold -> pause ramp, hold traffic for 10m, run deeper diagnostics (runtime logs, gpu metrics).
- Immediate rollback to previous routing map: if critical errors (>=0.5% absolute error spike or p99 > 2x baseline) -> run: deploy-tool rollback --routing-snapshot snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMM
- Fallback-only rollback: if model-quality regressions detected but infra signals fine -> revert routing to previous model variant while preserving batching changes.

Smoke tests (run after each phase change):
- Basic end-to-end: simple chat prompt sequence (tools/smoke/end2end_chat.sh) -> expect stable latencies and no inference errors.
- Tokenization sanity: run tokenizer roundtrip on sample corpus (10k tokens).
- KV cache sanity: check hit/miss counters pre and post warmers.
- Canary-specific: confirm canary hostgroup metrics exposed in Prometheus (labels: hostgroup=canary-AG-03).

Communications template (Slack announcement):
- Preflight (T-60m): "Afterglow deploy window starting in 60m. Shift lead: @Maya. Canary at T-15m (0.5%). See #release-afterglow for live updates. Linked runbook: CONFLUENCE-REL-5678"
- Phase changes: "Phase B ramp to 5% STARTED. Monitoring p50/p95/p99. @oncall"
- Abort/rollback: "ABORT: Rolling back afterglow canary to snapshot snapshot-YYYYMMDD-HHMM. Reason: p99 spike and 0.6% error delta. Owner: @Maya. Postmortem stub: CONFLUENCE-REL-5678/postmortem/XXXX"

Release notes (draft to paste into candidate changelog):
- Title: Afterglow: batching hint and KV warmers for tail-latency improvements
- Summary: Small runtime change that adjusts default batching hint for interactive workloads and introduces a synthetic warmer to prime KV caches after low-traffic periods. Expected improvements: reduced p99 latencies for short-chat patterns and small per-token cost savings in low-burst windows.
- Components touched: serving-runtime (batching engine), routing service (routing map JSON), optimize (batching profiles).
- Migration notes: No client changes. Operators should see new profile in console -> Optimize -> afterglow-8ms.
- Known issues: synthetic warmer may increase transient CPU on dedicated pools during warm-up; watch cost meters.

Post-flight checklist and initial retro prompts (T+120m):
- [ ] Consolidate telemetry snapshots (pre, mid, post) into release folder
- [ ] Fill in quick postmortem template (link above) if any warnings escalated
- [ ] Update canary config if thresholds were too strict/lenient
- [ ] Schedule follow-up with model team if quality drift observed

Retro prompt bullets (paste into Confluence):
- What signals were most useful? What was noisy?
- Did canary cadence feel right for the risk profile?
- Did batching profile deliver expected latency reductions?
- Were communication posts timely and adequate?
- Action items for next afterglow lane (owners + ETA)

Notes-to-self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Q: Should we bind warmers to low-priority compute instead of dedicated pool to reduce cost spikes? (Priya to prototype)
- Q: Is the default 8ms batch-window optimal for longer multi-turn chats? Need sweep across sample workloads.
- TODO: Add short CLI helper to snapshot/restore routing map and attach to deploy-tool (Owen).
- TODO: Add a small canary-quality evaluation that runs automatically when canary traffic >5% (Leo)

Appendix: quick commands
- Snapshot routing map: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/map > snapshot-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M).json
- Canary deploy: deploy-tool canary --group canary-AG-03 --config batching_hint=afterglow-8ms --traffic 0.5
- Rollback routing: deploy-tool rollback --routing-snapshot snapshot-20260312-2000.json
- Warm KV caches: bash tools/warm_kv_afterglow.sh --targets canary-AG-03 --rate 500/s --duration 5m

End of draft. Paste updated notes to CONFLUENCE-REL-5678 and add any retrospective owners.
